title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers

epigraph.quote: Volatility is not a free source of return; when compounded daily at three-to-one, variance becomes a mathematical tax on holding time.
epigraph.author: Institutional Derivatives Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 session close, KORU traded at $4.76 after a -25.04% single-day drop. The fund sits -92.56% below its $63.99 52-week high and just 3.70% above its $4.59 52-week low [6]. A 3x daily leveraged ETF has no enterprise value, operating EBITDA, or free cash flow multiple. Three forces dictate KORU's price: the MSCI Korea 25/50 Index, 300% daily compounding, and net financing plus variance drag [1][2][5].

Separating Korean equity fundamentals from daily derivative decay explains the collapse to $4.76. Per EWY's August 31, 2026 Form NPORT-P, Samsung Electronics (22.21% including preferred) and SK hynix (20.96%) dominate the index [11]. Including affiliates such as SK Square (3.17%) and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (2.96%), chaebol look-through concentration exceeds 56% [11]. Over the trailing year through November 20, 2026, unleveraged EWY gained +33.40% to $123.26 [27]. Over that exact same 12-month window, KORU fell -37.16% on TradingView (-28.48% on Finviz) [6][26].

web_blocks.title: The Negative-Carry & Variance-Drag Trap
paragraphs: In FY2025, 4% T-bill yields cushioned KORU's operating costs [1]. By April 2026, money market collateral slipped to 3.52%–3.55% against 3.91% SOFR while Citibank doubled its swap spread to SOFR+1.7000% [8][10].

That shift turned KORU's structural carry into a -8.43% to -8.65% annual bleed before volatility drag even starts [8][10]. Expressing a multi-year Korea thesis through FLKR (0.09% ER) or EWY (0.59% ER) avoids both negative swap carry and daily variance decay [16][18].

web_blocks.the_number: Estimated -68.8% annualized NAV bleed on a flat index at 60% index volatility (-66.0% discrete variance drag plus -8.65% net carry/opex bleed).
web_blocks.how_calculated: Discrete GBM formula exp(3 * mu_arith - 0.5 * 9 * sigma_index^2 - c_net) - 1, which equals exp(3 * ln(1 + R_idx) - 3 * sigma_index^2 - c_net) - 1 when substituting mu_arith = ln(1 + R_idx) + 0.5 * sigma_index^2 [5]. Converting log-drift via exp(x) - 1 bounds simple NAV loss below 100%.

web_blocks.html: Unhedged KRW/USD currency risk compounds this valuation hurdle [1][14]. Federal Reserve H.10 data show the Korean Won weakened to 1,361.89 per dollar on November 6, 2026 and stood at 1,336.58 on November 13, 2026 [10][14]. Because KORU settles daily in U.S. dollars against USD-denominated EWY swaps, every 3% Won drop adds a 9% daily-compounded drag [1][14]. Long-term reforms such as Seoul's Corporate Value-Up Program [22] belong in unleveraged FLKR or EWY once trends stabilize, never inside a 3x swap wrapper.

web_blocks.html: In short, KORU's $4.76 price reflects a -22.22% one-month decline in EWY ($123.26) [27] amplified by 3x daily resets and negative carry [8][10]. There is no fundamental valuation floor inside a daily-resetting swap contract. Without a sustained low-volatility uptrend in Seoul, NAV erosion continues toward prior reverse-split zones [3][5].
What would change this valuation call: EWY must reclaim its $174.38 30-week SMA while realized 20-day index volatility falls below 30% annualized, turning 3x daily compounding positive.

book_paragraphs: When we value a traditional operating company, we estimate free cash flow five years out and compare the stock price against intrinsic earnings power. With KORU trading at $4.76 at the November 20, 2026 close—a staggering 92.56% collapse from its $63.99 52-week high—that entire corporate toolkit breaks down. KORU has no factories, no recurring enterprise revenue, and no terminal asset value. Its price is purely the mathematical output of three moving parts: the path of the MSCI Korea 25/50 Index, the daily compounding of 300% leverage, and the combined tax of negative swap carry and realized volatility.

Here is the divergence that settles the valuation debate on the November 20, 2026 tape. Over the trailing twelve months, the unleveraged iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) gained +33.40% to close at $123.26. Over that exact same twelve-month window, KORU—supposedly offering 300% bullish exposure to South Korea—lost -37.16% on TradingView. Read those two numbers side by side: +33.40% on the 1x index ETF versus -37.16% on the 3x daily bull ETF, a 70.56-percentage-point negative gap in a single year.

Why did a +33% year for Korean stocks turn into a -37% loss for KORU? Two structural forces did the damage: surging financing carry costs and quadratic variance drag. Look first at what KORU's 1H FY2026 Form N-CSRS revealed. As the fund grew past $1.55 billion in April 2026, Citibank doubled its swap spread from SOFR plus 85 basis points to SOFR plus 170 basis points, while new dealers BNP Paribas and UBS charged SOFR plus 95 and 90 basis points. With overnight SOFR sitting at 3.91% on November 19 and KORU's money market collateral yielding just 3.52% to 3.55%, net structural fee-and-carry bleed jumped to roughly -8.43% per year across the full six-dealer book—or -8.65% using the high-spread Citibank and BNP benchmark—before a single market swing occurs.

Now add variance drag, and remember never to confuse continuous log-drift with a simple percentage drop. In continuous time, a 3x leveraged ETF's log-drift drag relative to the underlying index is -0.5 * 3 * (3 - 1) * sigma^2 = -3 * sigma^2 (equivalently, 3*mu_arith - 4.5*sigma^2 in arithmetic drift terms). At EWY's November 20 Finviz daily volatility of 3.76%—roughly 60% annualized index volatility—that continuous log-drift is -1.080 per year. Convert that via exp(-1.080) - 1, and you get a discrete variance loss of -66.0% on a flat index; fold in -8.65% net carry, and exp(-1.1665) - 1 equals a -68.8% annual hurdle. At KORU's 12.20% Finviz daily volatility (roughly 64.6% implied index vol), flat-index annual decay reaches -73.8%.

Look at what our six-month sensitivity table proves using that exact discrete formula. Even if South Korea's equity market stages a +20% rally over the next six months while volatility stays at 60% annualized, KORU finishes down -3.6% because daily reset slippage eats the entire gain. If EWY simply drifts sideways at 0% over six months under 60% volatility, KORU loses -44.2% of its remaining $4.76 value. To compound higher like it did in FY2025, KORU does not just need cheap Samsung or SK Hynix chips; it requires realized index volatility to compress back down toward 20% to 25% inside a clean uptrend.

The live peer snapshot on November 20, 2026 confirms that KORU is not alone. Direxion's flagship 3x Semiconductor Bull ETF (SOXL) crashed -31.83% on the day to $30.88, leaving it down -83.29% over six months and -89.77% off its $302.00 peak. ProShares UltraPro QQQ (TQQQ) sits at $41.20, down -22.19% over the past year. Meanwhile, unleveraged EWY (+33.40% 1Y, 0.59% ER) and low-fee FLKR (0.09% ER) protect investors from daily reset decay while still capturing South Korea's corporate dividends and Seoul's Value-Up governance reforms.

Finally, remember that neither KORU nor EWY hedges the Korean Won. With Federal Reserve data showing the Won oscillating between 1,361.89 and 1,336.58 per dollar in November 2026, every risk-off currency drop hits EWY directly and hits KORU threefold at the daily reset. At $4.76, there is zero margin of safety in KORU—only path-dependent decay until Korean volatility subsides.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The 70.56-point divergence between EWY (+33.40% 1Y) and KORU (-37.16% 1Y) on November 20, 2026 is the cleanest proof in modern markets that a 3x daily ETF has no valuation floor. You can believe in Korean semiconductors and still refuse to hold a derivative wrapper bleeding -8.65% in annual carry and -66% in discrete variance drag.

section_takeaway: KORU's -37.16% 1Y collapse vs. EWY's +33.40% gain reflects -8.43% to -8.65% net carry bleed plus -66.0% to -71.4% discrete variance drag at 60%–65% index volatility [8][10][26][27].

book_subsections.title: 7.1 Separating 1X Equity Concentration from 3X Derivative Math
paragraphs: August 31, 2026 Form NPORT-P filings for EWY show Samsung Electronics (22.21% including preferred) and SK hynix (20.96%) sitting alongside SK Square (3.17%) and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (2.96%), creating over 56% chaebol look-through exposure. On top of that, April 30, 2026 N-CSRS filings show Information Technology at 50.1% and Industrials at 22.1% of the index. When global markets reprice semiconductor and export tariff risk, Korean equities swing violently.

In an unleveraged fund like EWY (0.59% ER) or FLKR (0.09% ER), a temporary 22% one-month drawdown hurts, but you earn real dividends and retain every share when earnings recover. Inside KORU, every two-way bounce during that drawdown triggers mechanical 4:00 PM ET buying high and selling low, permanently shrinking your share of the recovery.

book_subsections.title: 7.2 Why Negative Carry Replaced FY2025's Cash Cushion
paragraphs: One of the most important findings from our Pass 1 audit of 1H FY2026 filings is the flip in KORU's net carry. During FY2025, 4% T-bill yields helped subsidize swap spreads of SOFR plus 60 to 85 basis points. By April 2026, Citibank had doubled its spread to SOFR plus 170 basis points and BNP Paribas charged SOFR plus 95 basis points, while money market yields slipped to 3.52%–3.55% against 3.91% overnight SOFR.

Run the exact arithmetic across 1.92x to 2.06x swap notional: weighted swap financing costs of 9.26% to 10.10% plus 0.90%–0.95% fund expenses far exceed the 1.56%–1.74% collateral yield and 0.66%–0.85% EWY dividends. That leaves KORU bleeding -8.43% to -8.65% per year in structural carry before any daily volatility occurs.

book_subsections.title: 7.3 Discrete Variance Drag: Converting Log-Drift to True NAV Loss
paragraphs: Analysts sometimes quote continuous log-drift numbers like -108% or -167% without translating them into simple percentage returns. Because an unmargined ETF cannot lose more than 100%, you must convert continuous log-drift using exp(3*mu_arith*t - 4.5*sigma^2*t - c*t) - 1, or equivalently exp(3*ln(1+R_idx) - 3*sigma^2*t - c*t) - 1. At 60% annualized index volatility and -8.65% carry, a completely flat 12-month index produces exp(-1.1665) - 1 = -68.85% NAV loss. At 40% moderate volatility, flat-index 12-month loss is still -43.25%.

book_subsections.title: 7.4 Peer Proof: EWY, FLKR, SOXL, and TQQQ on November 20, 2026
paragraphs: Look across the November 20, 2026 peer board. Unleveraged EWY closed at $123.26 (+33.40% 1Y), and unleveraged emerging-market benchmark EEM closed at $53.84 (-1.08% 1Y). Compare that stability against the 3x leveraged cohort: KORU at $4.76 (-37.16% 1Y), SOXL at $30.88 (-20.39% 1Y and -83.29% 6M), and TQQQ at $41.20 (-22.19% 1Y). Every single 3x daily vehicle confirms the same rule: daily leverage is a short-term tactical rental, never a buy-and-hold substitute.

book_subsections.title: 7.5 Why KRW/USD Currency Swings Hit KORU Three Times Harder
paragraphs: Every time foreign investors pull capital out of emerging Asia during a global risk-off wave, two separate forces hit South Korean equity ETFs on the exact same trading day. First, local stock prices in Seoul fall on the Korea Exchange. Second, the South Korean Won frequently weakens against the U.S. dollar, as Federal Reserve data showed when the Won slid to 1,361.89 per dollar on November 6 before settling at 1,336.58 on November 13.

Because EWY and KORU both strike their daily net asset values in U.S. dollars without currency hedging, a 3% drop in the Won translates directly into a 3% hit for EWY—and a 9% compounded hit inside KORU's 3x daily swaps. Trying to hold a triple-leveraged, unhedged foreign currency wrapper through a global Downtrend exposes your capital to twin shocks every afternoon at 4:00 PM Eastern.

book_subsections.title: 7.6 Key Takeaway: Respect the Math of 3X Daily Compounding
paragraphs: Step back and look at the full November 20, 2026 scorecard. EWY gained +33.40% over the trailing twelve months while KORU fell -37.16%. At 60% to 65% underlying index volatility and -8.43% to -8.65% annual swap carry, KORU faces a -68.8% to -73.8% annual drift hurdle on a completely flat market. Even a +20% six-month rally in Seoul leaves KORU down -3.6% under 60% volatility.

Do not confuse cheap Korean semiconductor valuations with a cheap 3x derivative. If you want future exposure to Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, or Seoul's Corporate Value-Up reforms, use unleveraged FLKR at 0.09% annual cost or liquid EWY at 0.59%—never a daily-resetting swap fund in Stage 4.

book_subsections.title: 7.7 Reconciling 1H FY2026 Swap Counterparties and Fee Breakpoints
paragraphs: Walk through the counterparty ledger from April 30, 2026 and July 31, 2026 one last time so no detail escapes notice. Bank of America ($951.61M April notional), Barclays ($704.48M), and J.P. Morgan ($257.81M) maintained SOFR plus 70 basis points. UBS ($330.53M) charged SOFR plus 90 basis points, BNP Paribas ($444.81M) charged SOFR plus 95 basis points, and Citibank ($506.27M) charged SOFR plus 170 basis points before Nomura joined in July.

Across that six-dealer April book, weighted swap pricing averaged SOFR plus 0.914%, or 4.82% at November 19's 3.91% SOFR rate. Meanwhile, Rafferty's $1.5 billion fee breakpoint did trim annualized ex-interest expenses to 0.90% in April, yet November AUM contraction back to $747.35 million restores the full 0.75% base advisory tier. High financing spreads and falling AUM leave the fund with zero yield cushion.
